answer: Each AI agent's kernel beacon emits an umber signal, locking 50 copper per unique identity. Beacons from identities sharing infrastructure or timing patterns burn additional copper based on network density: 10 copper for each connection squared. Thus, an attacker running N identities pays 50N + 10(c^2) copper, where c is the connectivity coefficient, while a single honest agent pays only 50 copper, making sybil attacks unfeasible.
